sourceRenderMethod.howTheSourceWasRendered: pdftoppm -r 600 -gray -png, Poppler 24.02.0, WITH ANNOTATIONS DRAWN. -hide-annotations was never passed on any measuring render, so the source render carries the widget /AP /N appearance ink whose absence from a delivered page the directional difference exists to detect. The delivered fixtures carry no AcroForm at all (pdfinfo Form: none; a pdf-lib enumeration returns 0 widgets), so every mark on a delivered page is content-stream ink and the annotation question arises only on the source side.
sourceRenderMethod.provenAtWholePageLevel: Pinned 600-00228 rendered both ways in this container at 600 dpi, grey<128: page 1 reads 1611695 dark with annotations against 1602354 with -hide-annotations (net 9341); page 2 reads 1236377 against 1231064 (net 5313).
sourceRenderMethod.provenAtWidgetLevelAndStrongerThanACrop: The net figure is not trusted, and it is not the whole truth: it is the difference of two directional counts. Decomposing the annotations-on / annotations-off difference onto EVERY source widget rectangle on the page (not four hand-picked 132x132 crops) gives, on page 1: annotations ADD 14085 dark pixels and COVER 4744, and 14085 = 3791 (f21) + 3688 (f22) + 3655 (f16) + 2951 (f15) and 4744 = 1178 + 1536 + 947 + 1083 exactly, with gain 0 and loss 0 OUTSIDE every widget rectangle on the page. Page 2: annotations add 7479 = 3791 (f72) + 3688 (f73) and cover 2166 = 1083 + 1083, again 0 and 0 outside every widget rect. A render that failed to draw /AP /N would have shown these as zero; a render drawing something else would have left a remainder outside the rects. There is no remainder.
sourceRenderMethod.thresholdSweptNotAssumed: Thresholds 96,104,112,120,128,136,144,160 at 600 dpi. The annotation gain is 14085 (p1) / 7479 (p2) at EVERY threshold in that range; the annotation loss is stable at 4744 / 2166 across 112-144. t=128 sits inside both plateaus and every figure in these rows is published at grey<128, 600 dpi unless stated.
sourceRenderMethod.thresholded: grayscale < 128 counted as dark; ADDED = dark in delivered and not in source, REMOVED = dark in source and not in delivered, reported PER PAGE.
sourceRenderMethod.whatTheAnnotationLossMeans: 4744 pixels on page 1 and 2166 on page 2 are dark WITHOUT annotations and light WITH them: the six selection widgets’ source-authored /AP /N /Off appearances paint over the court’s own printed ballot-box outline and redraw it. That is the source’s own behaviour, it is what a PDF viewer shows a participant, and it is the reason FIX130’s single net figure of 9341 understates what the annotation layer does. Reporting one net number for this page hides a 4744-pixel directional loss.
sourceRenderMethod.intermediatesDeleted: Every 600 and 300 dpi PNG rendered by this lane was deleted immediately after it was counted. None is left on disk and none is committed.

whyThisFails.notReadingOrder: Measured against widget geometry on the pinned bytes. On 200-00129 page 2 the new-charges table is three rows: row 1 f22(x52.89)/f23(x232.55)/f24(x340.25)/f25(x458.06) at y=[699.76,712.73]; row 2 f26w0/f27w0/f28/f29 at y=[685.57,698.52]; row 3 f30w0/f31w0/f32/f33 at y=[670.84,683.80]. whyThisFails.whatThatDoesOnThePage: Because the Address column (f27w1 x=252.26, f31w1 x=252.91) is emitted before the State Agency column (f26w1 x=53.62, f30w1 x=53.62), the delivered page prints 'Address (other state entities to notify) | that agency's address' ABOVE 'State Agency (other state entities to notify) | the name of any other state agency the court should notify'. The demonstrative 'that agency' precedes its antecedent, twice on 200-00129 page 2 and twice on 200-00132A page 1. Likewise 'the date that second new charge was brought' is the fifth item and 'a second new offence, if there is one' is the seventh.
whyThisFails.whyThisIsTheFactorysOwnStandard: FIX130 judged both conditions defects on five sibling families in this same shift, from this same corpus, and repaired them - recording that the bare caption 'leaves three consecutive rows all reading Description of Offense with only the what-to-write column to tell them apart', and that it re-emitted the items 'in reading order - page, then down the page, then across the row - because the committed list came out in field-tree order'. This family was held by the same lane in the same shift and did not receive that repair. Applying the factory's own standard consistently is what this FAIL asks for.
whyThisFails.whatThisIsNot: This is NOT a mis-mapping. All 48 items were checked against widget geometry on the pinned bytes and every one names the correct blank: 'the date that second new charge was brought' is f28, which is row 2; 'that second agency's address' is f31w1 at y=416.04, which is the second agency row.
